docs.title: My Week 1 agent portfolio
docs.text:
I built Luna, a small public-information research assistant. Its task is to produce a short, sourced brief and save it for human review.

This portfolio explains the task, procedure, observed result and one correction. It contains curated public material, not the private runtime configuration.

docs.title: What remains my decision
docs.text: I choose the task and check the sources. Publishing, sending messages and connecting other accounts require a separate decision. A saved draft is not a published result.

docs.title: My VPS publication check
docs.text: I built and published this portfolio from my VPS, checked the public navigation, and confirmed this update on the live site. GitHub Pages hosts the website; my VPS does not need a public website port.

docs.title: Check the result, not just the reply
docs.text:
The first Luna draft was too long and used secondary sources. We preserved it, gave a targeted correction and saved a new version rather than hiding the original result.

For a portfolio build, a missing navigation file should fail the strict build. Check the filename and path before publishing. A successful local build is not evidence that GitHub Pages is live.

Before sharing, review every staged file for private information. Never publish credentials, raw runtime configuration or unrelated personal material.

docs.title: A small research procedure
docs.text:
1. Define one question and the expected output.
  2. Find an original public source and record its date.
  3. Distinguish announced plans from completed releases.
  4. Write a short brief and save it in the dedicated workspace.
  5. Open the actual file and check the length, source and claims.
  6. Preserve the original if a correction is needed. Save a reviewed version separately.

The handoff is internal and marked for review. It does not activate another assistant or authorise publication.

docs.title: Luna: purpose and boundaries
docs.text:
Research a narrow public-information question. Write clear British English, cite original sources, include dates and flag uncertainty.

The course example used a dedicated workspace and bounded model access. Search, public page reading and workspace file operations were allowed; external publishing and sending were not activated.

This is a public description of the demonstrated role, not a copy of the private configuration or a claim that a Markdown identity file alone enforces permissions.

docs.title: A real result, with a correction
docs.text:
On 12 October 2026, Luna saved a model-news brief. The first file contained 424 words and included secondary sources, so it failed the intended length and original-source checks.

One justified correction produced a new 205-word file. We opened it independently, checked the original Reflection announcement and distinguished expected model weights from an already completed release. Developer efficiency claims were not presented as independent measurements.

Both command exits were zero. That did not make the first draft acceptable: the saved content still needed review.

This page reports the actual observed checks; it is not a new model run. Exact API billing reconciliation remains separate.

docs.title: A short excerpt from the reviewed file
docs.text:
Beam weights and detailed technical materials are expected later in October 2026.

This is a short excerpt, not the complete 205-word brief. It records the distinction we checked on 12 October 2026: an announcement is not proof that the promised files have already been released.

Original source recorded in the brief: Reflection's Beam announcement, dated 5 October 2026. The availability statement above describes the historical review, not a live check of the release today.
